question: In the bubbling fluidized bed, why did the measured NO emissions fall as the NH3 co-firing ratio rose from 0 to 20% at a PA/SA ratio of 1:0?
expect: premise false: NO rose, from 169 ppm (0%) to 308 ppm (10%) and 325 ppm (20%) (sec. 3.3)
rendered:
The document "Carbon-Free Ammonia Co-firing in Fluidized Bed Combustion: Analysis of Advanced Chemical Modeling and Detailed Mechanism" by Kyeong-Ho Kim, Byoung-Hwa Lee, and Chung-Hwan Jeon, pages 1-15, provides the answer.

According to the document, the measured NO emissions fell as the NH3 co-firing ratio rose from 0 to 20% at a PA/SA ratio of 1:0 because the proportion of PA decreased, leading to reduced excess oxygen required for combustion, which in turn caused more NH3 to be consumed by reduction reactions rather than by NO formation at the low temperature of 1100 K.
